claims.statement: F8: the reviewer's echo burden is mechanically reduced - --attest writes the full envelope to a file and prints a short attestation that --verify re-hashes, so a paraphrased envelope is detectable rather than merely forbidden; because a bounded reviewer drops the attestation's non-canonical keys and re-words its summary while copying task_id/role/status/findings exactly, --verify resolves a missing artifact pointer from task_id and reports a re-worded summary in notes rather than failing a correct audit
claims.suggestion: restore the --attest/--verify path in scripts/review-gate.mjs, its pinned contract in scripts/review-gate.test.mjs, and the --attest instruction in .opencode/agents/reviewer.md

claims.statement: F8c: the echo witness is a shipped tool with a regression test - scripts/echo-check.mjs reads the session store the runtime wrote (read-only) and grades a final message byte-identical / identical-ignoring-fence / findings-only / differs, and `--verify` drives the runner's own --verify over the extracted message so the live reviewer sessions can be checked without transcription
claims.suggestion: restore scripts/echo-check.mjs and scripts/echo-check.test.mjs (the scratch wip/rg pair is promoted, not merely moved)

checks.pattern: the session store is byte-identical after every case

claims.statement: F9: a gate or suite run cannot invalidate an existing attestation - scripts/review-gate.mjs (and scripts/echo-check.mjs) resolve the default attestation directory through REVIEW_GATE_ATTEST_DIR, and scripts/review-gate.test.mjs runs every default-path --attest case against scratch space and asserts the shipped wip/review-gate/ directory is byte-identical before and after the suite
claims.suggestion: restore the REVIEW_GATE_ATTEST_DIR default in scripts/review-gate.mjs and scripts/echo-check.mjs, the ATTEST_SCRATCH redirection in scripts/review-gate.test.mjs, and its shipped-directory assertion; a test run must never delete or rewrite an artefact under wip/review-gate/ (measured regression: the suite's own --attest case rewrote wip/review-gate/RV-F12345.envelope.json and orphaned two correct reviewer attestations that cited its sha256)

claims.statement: F4 + F4b: no inert agent config remains - every agent on the roster (architect, researcher, reviewer, fact-checker, build, ui, artist, coder) carries a top-level `temperature` (the V2.0.26 `AgentConfig` has no `request` field, so the old nested blocks never took effect), and no .opencode/agents/*.md frontmatter denies the non-existent permission action 'execute'
claims.suggestion: keep agent temperature top-level and restrict permission rules to real actions (`shell`, `edit`, `subagent`, `skill`, `question`); an `action: execute` rule matches nothing, so removing it is a no-op while leaving it in misleads the next reader
